entities.summary: Classical music generally refers to the art music of the Western world, considered to be distinct from Western folk music or popular music traditions. It is sometimes distinguished as Western classical music, as the term "classical music" can also be applied to non-Western art musics. Classical music is often characterized by formality and complexity in its musical form and harmonic organization, particularly with the use of polyphony. Since at least the ninth century, it has been primarily a written tradition, spawning a sophisticated notational system, as well as accompanying literature in analytical, critical, historiographical, musicological and philosophical practices.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Classical music has had a profound impact on Western culture and society, shaping the development of art, literature, and philosophy for centuries. Its influence can be seen in countless works of literature, art, and architecture, with many of its most famous composers continuing to be widely performed and studied today.
